Do not combine traversals into a net excursion. Second classify each ledger row independently. For that crossing, identify its departure and destination target sites, representative resting wrist positions at those endpoints, and intermediate wrist samples belonging to that crossing. Write any positions as [y, x]. Compute destination target x minus departure target x to determine horizontal direction; do not use a local reversal in wrist x. Judge the arc using the substantial interior wrist excursion relative to the line joining that row's endpoint wrist positions, not a near-arrival sample that may belong to the next crossing. For endpoint wrist positions [y0, x0] and [y1, x1] and an interior wrist sample [ys, xs], when x1 differs from x0, baseline_y = y0 + (y1 - y0) * (xs - x0) / (x1 - x0). Negative ys minus baseline_y indicates upper; positive indicates lower. Use wrist coordinates throughout this baseline calculation. Reversing horizontal direction does not by itself change the side of the baseline occupied by the arc. Independently check the intermediate wrist trajectory against the baseline joining that segment's endpoint wrist resting positions: upper selects D for smaller x or A for larger x; lower selects B for smaller x or C for larger x. Correct any letter that fails either check. Recheck both properties for every segment, including successive moves in the same horizontal direction and moves immediately after reversals; neither direction nor arc may be copied from a neighboring traversal. Write the full list at this first decision, without deleting the move selected now. On a later decision with carried memory, the intervening execution shows the preceding oracle command completed at its adjacent target; remove exactly one leading letter from the carried list before selecting the next command. The decision-step protocol guarantees that each such return follows one completed command, so do not count individual frames or repeated highlights as additional completions.
